title: Premji Invest, others invest $500 million in robotics startup Genesis AI at $3.5 billion valuation
summary: Robotics startup Genesis AI secures 500 million dollars from Premji Invest at a 3.5 billion valuation
detailed: Robotics startup Genesis AI raised $500 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures, and Eclipse at a $3.5 billion post-money valuation.
The funding brings the company's total disclosed funding to $605 million following a $105 million seed round in July 2025.
Headquartered in Paris and San Carlos, California, Genesis AI builds general-purpose robots, including its flagship headless robot Eno unveiled in June 2026.
The startup develops its foundation model (GENE), simulation platform (Genesis World), and hardware internally, and plans to use the capital for scaling data collection and manufacturing.
sentences: Robotics startup Genesis AI has raised $500 million in a Series A round co-led by Premji Invest, the family office of Wipro founder Azim Premji, Khosla Ventures and Eclipse, at a post-money valuation of $3.5 billion.

The startup, which is headquartered in Paris and San Carlos, California, has raised the funding to advance its development of general-purpose robots, with a particular focus on building robotic hands capable of handling objects in ways similar to humans.
Rowe Price Associates, French state-backed investor Bpifrance, HSG, Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Zoom, Samsung Next and Ericsson also took part.
Individual investors include former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Zoom CEO Eric Yuan, former Yahoo CEO Jerry Yang, French entrepreneur Xavier Niel and former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn.
The round values Genesis at about $3 billion before the new money.
It comes roughly 16 months after the company raised a $105 million seed round in July 2025, taking its total disclosed funding to $605 million.
For Premji Invest, the deal is a major overseas bet.

The firm has spent the past few years building a portfolio of AI companies, largely in the US.
Premji Invest has invested in 11 AI startups with a combined valuation of $43 billion, according to data from Tracxn cited in July.
A day before the Genesis announcement, Dreamteam, an AI-native CRM startup, said it had raised $53 million from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.
Founded in 2024, Genesis is led by CEO Zhou Xian and president Théophile Gervet, who first met while pursuing graduate studies at Carnegie Mellon University.
Gervet previously worked as a researcher at French AI company Mistral AI.
The startup has a workforce of nearly 100 employees.
It develops its training data, its AI model, its simulator and its robot hardware together.
Its foundation model is called GENE, and its simulation platform, Genesis World, lets developers test robots across millions of virtual scenarios.
The startup designs its own actuators, motors, gearboxes and hands, and uses Nvidia chips for computing.
“ The model architecture contributes to maybe 10% of the final result, ” Zhou said, putting the weight instead on infrastructure and data quality.
He told the publication that hardware and supply chains remain the main bottleneck to scaling, and that the robot's dexterous hands currently need replacing after several weeks of regular work.
“ Our mission is to remove the physical limits on human ambition, ” Zhou said in the announcement.

“ By building it all ourselves, we can obsess over every detail and improve the entire robot faster in one closed loop. ”
Genesis unveiled its flagship robot, Eno, in June 2026.
The headless robot features a wheeled base, an extendable body and two arms equipped with human-sized dexterous hands.
The startup has built around 30–40 units and is testing the robot with select customers, including through a partnership with South Korea's LG CNS for manufacturing and logistics applications.

Genesis said it will use the capital to expand data collection and large-scale training, improve the range and complexity of tasks its system can handle, deploy Eno at scale and hire AI researchers, robotics experts and engineers.
Zhou said the startup is prioritising the US first, with a US supply chain, American contract manufacturers and customers, before expanding more broadly in Europe.
A contract manufacturer will begin mass production in the US next year, and Genesis expects a wider customer rollout in 2027, starting with factories, warehouses and laboratories.

Genesis joins a group of Europe-based robotics companies valued at more than $1 billion and aimed at industrial work, including Britain's Humanoid and Germany's Neura Robotics, Agile Robots and RobCo.
Agile Robots raised $500 million at an $8.5 billion valuation in a round led by SoftBank earlier this month.
Global venture funding to robotics startups reached $9.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, more than double the $4.3 billion invested a year earlier, according to Crunchbase data.
